What one event changed the trajectory of your life?

Gonna get laughed at for saying this, but may as well: when my parents bought me my first computer.

If not for this, I'm fairly sure I'd have died quite a while back. I had pretty blatant Asperger's as a child which wasn't diagnosed until relatively recently (2 years ago - I'm 21 years old now). Not having the innate social skills to really converse or relate to other children (it didn't help that my parents were too "busy" to really talk to me and help me with that) pretty much meant isolation apart from one "friend" who mainly used me as a circus owner would a dancing bear.

Most people refuse to believe me about this, but loneliness and bullying at ages 8-9 made me walk, alone, around the school at lunch breaks mumbling to myself the mantra "I wish I would die". I was too young to know what suicide was, and I think I remember feeling something of a "eureka moment" when I realised I could cause my existence to end.

Pretty much around this time however, I think my parents realised I was a pretty fucked up kid considering I had barely any friends and like any responsible parent would do, decided I didn't need any kind of intervention and bought me a PC.

Well, this act of denial gave me hope. Video games, the internet and various programs installed made a great coping method to deal with bullying that pretty much only stopped in the last two years of my non-university education. Oh, not that some kind of intervention to teach me social skills wouldn't have been great on the part of my parents. But getting a means to escape from my day-to-day suffering certainly changed the trajectory of my life.

NOTE 1: Yeah sorry this is rather maudlin. Planned to have this buried, didn't realise I'm the first to comment.

NOTE 2: Not a dumb "it gets better" comment, I now have Bipolar DIsorder and repressed childhood memories because of bullying/isolation. Having a coping method still staved off my suicidal desires, though (up until early adulthood, anyway).
